title: Gate-Controlled Spin Qubits in Confined Altermagnets
abstract: We propose gate-defined spin qubits in electrostatically confined altermagnetic quantum dots. Elliptical confinement of the $d$-wave altermagnetic structure produces a low-energy doublet with opposite spin polarization. For the range of parameters used here, the qubit states energy gap lies in the microwave range while the leakage gap remains in the meV range. Even without spin-orbit coupling, time-dependent simulations show that a phase-controlled quadrupolar gate drive about a fixed bias point implements $X_{π/2}$ and $X_π$ rotations by resonantly modulating the confinement anisotropy. We extend the study to two-qubits using a double quantum dot. We show that the double quantum dot spectrum can be cleanly projected onto isolated quantum dot product states with a nonzero nonlocal Pauli block in the effective logical two-qubit Hamiltonian. Resonant central-barrier modulation then drives the logical two-qubit component close to a maximally entangled state. These calculations show anisotropic altermagnetic quantum dots as a route to locally gate-controlled spin qubits without requiring spin-orbit coupling.
summary: The authors propose using spin qubits confined in altermagnetic quantum dots as a novel route to gate control. By exploiting the momentum-dependent spin splitting inherent to altermagnets, they demonstrate high-fidelity single and two-qubit gates purely through electrostatic confinement modulation. This work is significant because it offers a pathway for solid-state quantum computation that circumvents the need for problematic spin-orbit coupling terms.
main_problem: The paper proposes using gate-defined spin qubits within electrostatically confined altermagnetic quantum dots to achieve local, controlled qubit operations without relying on spin-orbit coupling.
main_result: They demonstrate that anisotropic altermagnets allow for arbitrary single-qubit rotations and coherent two-qubit entanglement generation by modulating the confinement anisotropy or interdot barrier, respectively.
method: The study employs atomistic real-space tight-binding models combined with time-dependent simulations and truncated Configuration Interaction (CI) methods to calculate quantum dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is based on electrons confined in altermagnetic quantum dots (single or double). The Hamiltonian incorporates hopping terms derived from the d-wave altermagnetic structure, confinement potentials ($	ext{HV}$), and time-dependent gate drives.
key_observables: Single-qubit: Qubit energy gap ($\sim$ microwave range) and spin polarization. Two-qubit: Logical concurrence ($C_{	ext{log}}$) and Bell fidelity ($F_{	ext{Bell}}$).
important_parameters: Ellipticity parameter $\delta$, gate drive amplitude ($A_Q$), detuning ($\epsilon$), and central barrier modulation strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on an idealized elliptical confinement model, and the control mechanism is shown to function without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic setups for single/double dots, show qubit splitting vs. ellipticity ($\delta$), and detail time evolution dynamics showing high fidelity in both single-qubit rotations and two-qubit Bell state preparation.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical platform using elliptical confinement to create a spin doublet. It then details single-qubit control via resonant quadrupolar driving, followed by an extension to double quantum dots where central-barrier modulation drives the system into maximally entangled two-qubit states.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, solid-state platform for realizing qubits whose fundamental operations (single and two-qubit gates) are governed purely by magnetic structure engineering rather than relying on SOC or external fields in complex ways.

For the single-qubit device, differential RF voltages modu- late the quadrupolar confinement anisotropy around a fixed elliptical bias point. For the two-qubit device, two locally anisotropic gates define left and right dots, while a central barrier gate sets the static interdot coupling and supplies res- onant barrier modulation.
